description-proc.fra: Le présent marché public est un marché de fournitures portant sur l’acquisition de biens relatifs à la fourniture, la livraison, l’installation, les essais, la mise en service et la formation des utilisateurs concernant un (1) système de navigation chirurgicale et deux (2) consoles médicales plafonnières destinés au complexe chirurgical de l’Hôpital clinique régional de Kyiv, en Ukraine. Le contractant devra fournir l’ensemble des équipements, logiciels, accessoires, éléments de fixation, licences et composants auxiliaires nécessaires afin de garantir des systèmes complets et pleinement opérationnels. Le marché comprend également le transport jusqu’au site du projet, le déchargement, l’installation, l’intégration des systèmes, les essais fonctionnels, la mise en service, la fourniture de la documentation ainsi que la formation du personnel clinique et technique. Tous les équipements devront être neufs, non utilisés, conformes aux normes internationales applicables aux dispositifs médicaux et fournis avec une garantie ainsi que des services d’assistance après-vente. Lieu de livraison : Complexe chirurgical de l’Hôpital clinique régional de Kyiv, Kyiv, Ukraine.
description-proc.eng: This public contract is a supply contract for the purchase of goods pertaining to the supply, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning, and user training of one (1) Surgical Navigation System and two (2) Medical Ceiling Consoles for the Surgical Complex of the Kyiv Regional Clinical Hospital, Ukraine. The scope of the contract includes transportation to the project site, unloading, installation, system integration, functional testing, commissioning, documentation, and training of clinical and technical personnel. title-proc.eng: Supply, Delivery and Installation of a Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) Suite consisting of 2 TEM tools and 1 Focused Ion Beam–Scanning Electron Microscope (FIB.SEM) for Tyndall Instit, UCC,

description-proc.eng: Tenders are sought for the Supply, Delivery and Installation of a Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) Suite, to Tyndall National Institute, University College Cork (UCC) comprising three complementary instruments: 1. One (1) Aberration-corrected and monochromated TEM 2. One (1) 200 kV high-throughput TEM 3. One (1) Focused Ion Beam–Scanning Electron Microscope (FIB-SEM) This procurement will establish a nationally significant microscopy capability for Ireland, strengthening Tyndall’s leadership in semiconductor, photonic, and quantum materials research and supporting long-term collaboration with academic and industrial stakeholders. The TEM Suite will deliver sustained scientific, technological, and economic impact through enhanced analytical capability, research excellence, and innovation at the nanoscale. This investment will expand and modernise Tyndall’s capability in advanced materials and device characterisation to meet the requirements of its national and international research programmes, including activities under the EU Chips Act and strategic collaborations with academic and industrial partners. The TEM Suite will form a key component of the new Tyndall laboratory facilities currently under development and will support Tyndall’s mission to provide world-leading infrastructure for semiconductor, photonic, and quantum technologies. The Aberration-corrected and monochromated TEM will represent the highest-performance instrument within the suite. It must deliver sub-ångström imaging resolution and high-energy-resolution spectroscopy, providing the capability to study interfaces, defects, and nanostructures at the atomic scale. The system must support advanced analytical and imaging modes, including low-dose operation for beam-sensitive materials, Lorentz and 4D-STEM imaging, and in-situ experimentation (electrical, thermal, and environmental). Automated alignment, optical stability, and full integration with advanced camera, detector, and control software are essential to ensure repeatable and high-quality data generation across multiple users. The 200 kV high-throughput TEM capable of atomic resolution imaging will provide a complementary, multi-user analytical capability to support daily research operations and routine analysis. It must combine high brightness and excellent spatial resolution with rapid operational stability, user-friendly alignment, and automated workflow functionality. This instrument will be optimised for versatility and efficiency, ensuring broad accessibility for internal and collaborative research, training, and industry engagement activities. The FIB-SEM will enable site-specific sample preparation, 3D structural analysis, and nanoscale milling to support both TEM systems. It must achieve high-resolution imaging and precision ion-beam milling for lamella production and cross-sectional analysis. Integration with the TEM workflows is required to ensure seamless specimen transfer and preparation from wafer-scale structures to atomic-scale analysis. This tender is being issued as a single integrated suite rather than as separate tools to ensure technical, operational, and economic coherence across all instruments. Procuring the TEMs and FIB-SEM from a single manufacturer will enable a shared control software platform, providing a consistent user interface and operational framework across the suite. This is important in Tyndall’s multi-user research and training environment, for staff, postgraduate students, and industry partners, as it simplifies training, improves safety, and promotes efficient use of laboratory time. A unified suite will also allow for the interchange of sample holders and accessories, enabling seamless workflow integration from sample preparation to atomic-scale imaging. A single-supplier arrangement provides additional benefits including simplified warranty and maintenance agreements, harmonised service schedules, and a single point of technical contact.

title-proc.eng: Transport respirator for Helse Førde HF

description-proc.eng: Helse Førde Health Trust intends to make a direct procurement of Hamilton 4 T1 transport respirators. A procurement contract will be signed with Medidyne AS, as well as an accompanying framework agreement for equipment dependent consumables. The contract also includes options for both 4 Hamilton C1 and 1 Hamilton MR1. The procurement has been started based on a replacement need where 4 transport respirators must be replaced due to an advanced age. Safety: When using different platforms for critical medical equipment, such as transport respirators, considerable safety risks can occur for patients, even in daily operation. In order to ensure a seamless transfer of respirator patients between local hospitals and internal movement between intensive care and other departments, it is crucial for transport that the respirator has the same user interface as the existing respirator park (Hamilton). This allows for quick and safe transmission of patients. Different respirators have different platforms and user interface, which can lead to confusion, wrong use and delays in lifesaving treatment. Transporting intensive care patients is already challenging and we would therefore like to avoid having different equipment for the same purpose in order to reduce the risk of user errors. Uniform equipment minimises the risk of errors and increases efficiency in critical situations. Improper use can lead to serious complications and potential deaths. In stand-by situations such as pandemics or other crises, it is necessary that all equipment is known to personnel. Standardisation: The remaining equipment of respirators in Helse Førde (Førde Central Hospital, Lærdal Hospital and Nordfjordeid Hospital) is from Hamilton. After the replacement there are no respirators of other brands in daily operation at Helse Førde. In order to ensure patient safety, it is decisive to use uniform platforms that are similar to the existing respirators. Training: With up to approx. 150 employees who want to use the transport conspirators irregularly, it is decisive to have a standardised platform in order to provide reliable training and maintenance of training to both users and service personnel. Training on different types of equipment will require significantly more time and resources and will result in an increased risk of improper use. By having a uniform platform, the training can be streamlined, ensuring that all users are comfortable and competent with the equipment. This is particularly critical in emergencies, where correct and rapid use of respirators can determine patients' health. The contracts will be signed without a prior competition notice as, according to what the contracting authority knows, there are no other suppliers of the concrete transport respirator from Hamilton. Pursuant to the procurement without competition is the Public Procurement Regulations § 13-4 letter b. 2. An intention notice is published in accordance with the provision in § 21-5. The contract will be signed 10 days at the earliest after an intention notice has been published.

The transport ́s direct emissions are obviously the most important part of the contract ́s total environmental impact. For example, a diesel vehicle with emissions of approx. 200 g CO₂/km and an annual driving length of 40,000 km will generate approx. 8 tonnes of CO₂ per annum. Hydrogen and battery electrical vehicles have zero direct emissions in the operational phase, while biogas vehicles in the lifetime perspective provide very low, and in some cases net negative, CO₂-equivalent emissions. The requirement gives a significant and substantiated reduction in total emissions over the contract ́s lifetime. The contracting authority has considered using climate and the environment only as the award criteria. Such a model would, however, only give a relative ranking between the tenders, without ensuring that the delivery is actually low- or zero-emission based. If prices or other criteria are weighted higher, fossil-based solutions can still win the competition. Furthermore, evaluating environmental performance involves methodology challenges connected to documentation, calculation assumptions (e.g. well-to-wheel vs. tank-to-wheel), inspections and verifiability, which can increase the risk of doubt. The minimum requirement reduces this risk by determining a clear and objective level for acceptable environmental performance. The requirement is justifiable, proportional and connected to the delivery. The market can deliver sufficient competition within the stipulated frameworks. The assessments listed above document the environmental, technical and legal considerations that form the basis for choosing requirements, and fulfil the contracting authority ́s justification obligation in accordance with the Public Procurement Act §5b.

description-proc.eng: Short description of the project: Just and Climate Resilient Urban Development and Decentralisation (CitiZen+D) CitiZen+D is a technical cooperation project financed by the Federal Ministry of Economic Development and Cooperation of Germany and implemented by GIZ in Zambia. The objective of the project is to support urban development in selected cities in Zambia with an emphasise on climate resilience, social inclusion, and sustainable financing, setting best practice for the whole country. Context In Zambia, increasing numbers of people are moving to cities, posing a major challenge for these urban centres. Tight budgets, complicated regulations and unclear responsibilities in planning and development result in a lack of adequate urban planning. This particularly affects temporary, poor settlements in and around cities. The population here has only limited access to public services such as waste disposal, fresh water and sanitation, and safe road planning. Disadvantaged groups such as women, children, people with disabilities and people living in poverty are especially hard hit. Environmental pollution and social problems also result. Approach The project advises selected cities on planning, coordinationng and implementationing of socially just and climate-friendly urban development. This allows the cities to realise development plans created in the earlier project phase and incorporate specific financing and operating arrangements into these plans. The project promotes cooperation between civil society, governmental institutions, organised interest groups and business to enable broad-based, socially just and future-oriented development in cities. The project aims for the population to have a say in planning and design, bolstering promoting trust in democratic institutions. Traditional authorities are also involved in the project. Locally successful approaches provide an example for other cities and feed into national aspects such as laws and guidelines. This should also result in administrative decentralisation. The project is part of the "Responsible Governance in Zambia" German development cooperation programme.

description-proc.eng: The project Strengthening Reproductive Health and Empowerment of Young Women (SRHEYW) is a module of German Development Cooperation in the health sector in Tanzania. It is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in cooperation with the Ministry of Health (MoH) and the Prime Minister"s Office - Regional Administration and Local Government (PMORALG). The project is implemented from July 2026 to June 2029 and focuses on Tanga Region. Despite progress in women"s rights and access to health services, many young people in Tanzania, particularly adolescent girls and young women, continue to face significant barriers to exercising their sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR). Persistent gender norms, unequal power relations, limited access to reliable information, high rates of adolescent pregnancy, unmet need for family planning, gender-based violence, and unequal access to services for young people with disabilities continue to undermine reproductive autonomy and health outcomes. The project aims to improve the reproductive autonomy and health of young women and newborns in selected areas of Tanzania. It focuses on strengthening maternal, neonatal, and reproductive health services; empowering young people with the knowledge and skills needed to make informed decisions regarding their sexual and reproductive health; improving the social and institutional environment that influences these decisions; and increasing access to SRHR services for people with disabilities. The intervention targets adolescent girls and young women while also engaging boys and young men, parents, teachers, religious and community leaders, health workers, civil society organisations, and government institutions. Particular attention is given to vulnerable groups, including young people living with disabilities and out-of-school youth. The project combines interventions at individual, community, institutional, and societal levels. Through youth clubs, community dialogue processes, social and behaviour change communication campaigns, and support to local civil society organisations, the project seeks to create an enabling environment in which young people can access information, utilise services, exercise their rights, and make informed choices about their future.

title-proc.eng: Digitalised rules for the road and transport sector - early dialogue

description-proc.eng: The Norwegian Public Roads Administration currently develops and administers comprehensive rules - laws, regulations, road norm templates, agreements, guidelines and individual decisions - without a joint system for development, management and disclosure. This limits the possibilities for taking out gains in the value chains where the regulations are developed, administered and used. The Norwegian Public Roads Administration is therefore carrying out a concept phase in 2026 in order to uncover the possibility room for a digitalised, machine-readable and machine-runnable regulations for the road and transport sector. The concept phase shall highlight how the regulations can be facilitated for seamless digital regulations, which types of rules, standards and formats a future system ought to support, as well as experiences and existing systems in the market. The results shall form the basis for the concept and requirement specifications in a planned main procurement in 2027, i.a. as a detachment for the current Vegnormal system. As part of the concept phase, the market is invited to an early dialogue in a digital dialogue conference 28 October 2026, an option for written input (deadline 11 November 2026) and any one-to-one meetings in week 47/48. The main target group is suppliers and R&D actors who can contribute input to systems that respond to the needs of rule managers, providers of digital services, case officers and users of the regulations. Further information on the contracting authority ́s needs, as well as a programme and registration for the conference are in the attached invitation. The dialogue conference will be held in Norwegian.
